# Signature fixtures

* `pyhanko-*.pdf`, `signer.cer`, `tsa.cer`: produced by **pyHanko 0.38.0** (`python generate_pyhanko_fixtures.py`; needs pikepdf and cryptography). Throw-away self-signed keys, not kept. The timestamp token comes from pyHanko's `DummyTimeStamper` with a local TSA certificate (no real TSA), so it proves structure and imprint handling, not a real authority. `pyhanko-pades-dss.pdf` embeds a self-signed chain with no revocation data (fetching disabled, soft-fail).
* `lib/`: produced by this library (`PDF_SECURITY_OUT=<dir> dotnet test tests/AdoBye.Tests -c Release --filter FullyQualifiedName~Export_docmdp_samples`) and validated with `python validate_with_pyhanko.py <dir>`; pyHanko's verdicts are recorded in `lib/pyhanko-0.38.0-results.txt`.
* `SignatureInteropTests` reads all of these by default; Python is only needed to regenerate.

Known differences: pyHanko reports `modification_level=LTA_UPDATES` rather than `FORM_FILLING` for the encrypted certified sample (its own classification of the update); `docmdp_ok` agrees. pyHanko says its diff policy was "not designed" for DocMDP level 3, though it accepted every P3 sample.

## PAdES / trust fixtures (`pades/`)

* `pyhanko-pades-*.pdf`, `root.cer`, `pyhanko-pades-revoked.crl`, `manifest.json`: produced by **pyHanko 0.38.0** (`python pades/generate_pades_fixtures.py`; throw-away EC keys, TSA key RSA because pyHanko's DummyTimeStamper is RSA-only). B-B, B-LT (signature timestamp + DSS), B-LTA (plus archive document timestamp) and a certificate that a synthetic CRL revokes one hour after signing. `PadesInteropTests` verifies them with `PdfSignatureTrust` at fixed instants (no network, no Python needed). `pyhanko-fixture-self-check.txt` records pyHanko's own verdicts (its `ades_lta_validation` passes the LTA file and reports NO_POE for the LT file, as expected).
* Library to pyHanko: `PDF_SECURITY_OUT=<dir> dotnet test tests/AdoBye.Tests -c Release --filter FullyQualifiedName~Export_pades_samples` then `python pades/validate_pades_with_pyhanko.py <dir>`; the verdicts of the last run are in `pades/lib-pyhanko-0.38.0-results.txt`. pyHanko reports intact/valid/trusted for every library file (CAdES with RSA PKCS#1 SHA-512, RSA-PSS SHA-384, ECDSA P-256/P-384/P-521, a certification signature, DSS, signature timestamp, document timestamp). Its stricter ETSI EN 319 102-1 `ades_lta_validation` returns Indeterminate (NO_POE) for the library's DSS/LTA files, with and without an intermediate CA, so full PAdES B-LT/B-LTA conformance is not independently confirmed.

### Exact guarantee of `PdfTrustStatus.Valid`

`Valid` means: the signature is intact over its ByteRange; the signer certificate path (RFC 5280 basic constraints, name/path-length limits, validity) reaches a caller-configured anchor (or the system store if enabled) as of the validation time; signer key usage / EKU / policy requirements hold; and, unless the policy relaxes it, every non-anchor certificate has authenticated CRL/OCSP evidence covering that time. The validation time is a fixed policy time, else the genTime of a timestamp (signature-time-stamp attribute or later document timestamp) accepted only if its TSA certificate is not the signer's own, has exactly one critical timeStamping EKU, is valid at genTime, chains to an anchor, is not revoked at genTime (revocation evidence required per policy), and whose CMS signature and message imprint verify; else now. A signer-claimed signingTime is used only on opt-in. `Valid` does not mean the signer's identity is legally qualified, that the document content is unmodified beyond what DocMDP/FieldMDP findings report, or full PAdES B-LT/B-LTA conformance.
